prompt: Use the limit definition of the derivative to find $f'(2)$ for $f(x) = \frac{1}{x}$. Give your answer as a fraction.
hint: Set up $\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\frac{1}{2 + h} - \frac{1}{2}}{h}$. Combine the two fractions on top first.

hints.text: Set up $\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\frac{1}{2 + h} - \frac{1}{2}}{h}$. Combine the two fractions on top first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $\frac{1}{2 + h} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2 - (2 + h)}{2(2 + h)} = \frac{-h}{2(2 + h)}$. Notice an $h$ appeared on top, ready to cancel.
Divide that by $h$: $\frac{-h}{2(2 + h) \cdot h} = \frac{-1}{2(2 + h)}$. Now let $h \to 0$.

explanation: Let $h \to 0$: $f'(2) = \frac{-1}{4}$. The tangent at $(2, \frac{1}{2})$ slopes gently downward.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity check with secants
steps: Heading to $-0.25 = -\frac{1}{4}$. Negative makes sense: $\frac{1}{x}$ decreases as $x$ grows.
